sections.title: Quality engineering

backgroundImage.alt: Continuous software testing and release assurance

sections.heading: Assure every release—from application change to AI-generated code
sections.body:
Frequent releases and AI-generated change need risk-based coverage, automated regression and accountable release decisions. We bring quality and security gates into CI/CD; [testoriumz](/products-and-accelerators/testoriumz) supports test management, low-code automation, AI root-cause analysis and dashboards.

Baseline validation lead time, critical-journey coverage and escaped defects—not a blanket quality promise. [Discuss release assurance](#get-in-touch).

sections.heading: Quality and security gates across CI/CD

items.description: Baseline risk — Identify critical journeys, AI-code scope and failure impact. Client release owners agree coverage, test environments, permitted data and acceptance thresholds.
Design maintainable packs — Plan regression, API, performance and user validation. Define traceability, suite ownership and quality/security gates before execution.
Execute and triage — Trace results to changes and investigate causes with testoriumz where appropriate. Combine relevant VectorX findings and Cyber-Safe Delivery controls; assign remediation owners.
Review and improve — Present release evidence, residual risks and exceptions to the accountable approver. Maintain test packs and measure escaped defects and validation cycle time after handover.

sections.heading: Evidence for the release decision
sections.body:
A release review should receive coverage against critical journeys, traced execution results, defect status, security findings and accepted exceptions. The accountable release owner decides whether agreed gates have been met; testing does not remove every risk.

Compare regression coverage, defect escape and validation lead time with the agreed baseline. Record toolchain, release scope and measurement period, and retain a redacted evidence pack for delivery governance.

See [Our approach and commercial models](/company/our-approach) for delivery governance and engagement details.

sections.heading: Plan the right engagement
sections.description: Use Fixed Price for a defined release-assurance scope, or Time & Materials for discovery and evolving coverage. A Dedicated Team supports sustained quality engineering; Managed Service can cover managed quality or a testing centre of excellence. Outcome-Based terms require measurable assurance baselines and attribution.

items.title: Can you work with our pipeline and testing tools?
items.description: Assess the existing CI/CD toolchain, environments, test data and coverage before agreeing integration. Preserve useful tooling where it fits; select testoriumz based on the required workflow and product fit.

items.title: How is AI-generated code assured?
items.description: Make AI-written change visible in scope, review its behaviour and dependencies, and test critical journeys. Combine quality gates with code and supply-chain analysis where appropriate; assign remediation and release approval.

items.title: Who sets and approves release gates?
items.description: Business, engineering, quality and security owners agree thresholds and exception handling. An accountable release owner reviews evidence and residual risks before approving deployment.

items.title: Can we buy testoriumz without a services project?
items.description: Yes. Linkfields software is available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without a services engagement. Confirm the product, deployment and commercial fit for your environment.

items.title: What should we bring to the conversation?
items.description: Share application and release scope, the current toolchain, regression risks and use of AI-generated code. We can agree assessment access, confidentiality and the assurance approach.
